open_points.subject: execution disclosure class with no values
open_points.text: “The class of an execution is the highest class among the values and files its NodeExecution or TrialExecution names as inputs … and for an operation also among its outputs” gives no result when both sets are empty.
open_points.question: What disclosure class does an inputless execution with no outputs, or one that fails before producing outputs, have?
options: Treat the empty maximum as `open`.
Use the binding’s declared output classes for an operation even when no output exists.
Refuse or leave the execution class undefined.

open_points.subject: redacted failure-detail length
open_points.text: “A `failure_detail` whose class is above `open` … is returned to an agent only as its length and that class.”
open_points.question: Is the disclosed length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit?
options: UTF-8 byte length.
Unicode code-point count.
Length after truncation in implementation-native characters.
open_points.default_guess: Use the UTF-8 byte length after the bounded failure detail has been formed.

open_points.subject: mapped many-file disclosure record
open_points.text: A13 says “the reference naming [a file list] carries the list’s class” and that an empty list “is named, with its class, by the one NodeExecution,” while M23 says file inputs and outputs are only “SpooledFiles by their facts”; an empty file list has no SpooledFile facts at all.
open_points.question: Where is the aggregate disclosure class of a mapped `many` file output represented durably, especially for an empty list, so recovery and disclosure checks can reproduce it?
options: Add class metadata to the file-list reference in NodeExecution.
Derive non-empty list classes from elements and add explicit class metadata only for empty lists.
Do not preserve an aggregate list class and classify only individual SpooledFiles.
open_points.default_guess: Represent the aggregate class on the file-list reference, including an explicit empty-list reference.

open_points.subject: agent view of mixed-class file lists
open_points.text: A13 says a mapped file list has the highest class among its elements and that each SpooledFile keeps its own class, while A07 only says “The same holds for a `personal_data` file.”
open_points.question: When a file list’s aggregate class is `personal_data` but some member SpooledFiles have lower classes, does an agent lose size, media type and spool facts for every member or only for members individually marked `personal_data`?
options: Redact every member when the list reference is `personal_data`.
Redact only members whose own SpooledFile class is `personal_data`.
Return only one digest and class for the entire list.
open_points.default_guess: Redact every member when viewed through a `personal_data` list reference, while separately viewed producer records follow each file’s own class.

open_points.subject: credential value normalization and HTTP bytes
open_points.text: A17 says a secret file’s content is “decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline” and rejects “a control character,” then says the value “is added as that header”; A09 searches response bytes for “the bytes of the credential value sent.”
open_points.question: Exactly which trailing newline is removed, which characters count as control characters, and how is an accepted non-ASCII Unicode value encoded into HTTP header bytes and into the credential-echo byte sequence?
options: Remove one LF, reject all Unicode control-category characters, and send UTF-8 bytes.
Remove one LF or CRLF, reject ASCII C0/C1 controls, and send UTF-8 bytes.
Restrict credentials to visible ASCII and reject every non-ASCII value.
open_points.default_guess: Remove one trailing LF or CRLF, reject C0/C1 control characters, and encode the remaining value as UTF-8 bytes consistently for sending and echo detection.

open_points.subject: credential-header collision start check
open_points.text: A09 says a credential header colliding with a selected instance’s required header “refuses to start,” while manifest operations and instance facts are otherwise read on demand and no rule says what startup does when the relevant manifest record, revision, service, or selected instance cannot be read.
open_points.question: What must startup do when it cannot obtain the manifest instance facts needed to perform the mandatory credential-header collision check?
options: Refuse startup whenever the selected instance facts cannot be read.
Start and defer all instance validation, including collisions, to proposal or send time.
Check collisions only for readable instances and ignore unreadable ones until use.
open_points.default_guess: Refuse startup because the required collision check cannot be completed safely.

open_points.subject: secret returned in another encoding
open_points.text: State 0 says service credentials “never enter … an answer,” but A17 says a service response carrying the credential “in another encoding is not recognised, and is protected only by its class,” allowing that content to be stored and returned.
open_points.question: Does the no-secret-in-an-answer guarantee cover semantic or encoded representations of a credential, or only the exact credential byte sequence?
options: Cover only the exact byte sequence; encoded representations may be returned according to disclosure class.
Cover recognizable encodings as well and withhold them.
Preserve State 0’s absolute guarantee and prevent any credential-derived response content from being returned.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the enforceable rule to the exact sent byte sequence only, and explicitly narrow the earlier absolute wording.

open_points.subject: ordering forced node conclusions against executable nodes
open_points.text: A13 defines the next executable node as the ready node with the smallest `node_id`; A15 orders records for nodes that “become non-executable together,” but neither text orders skipped or `upstream_failed` conclusions relative to ready node executions or defines which transitive conclusions become non-executable together.
open_points.question: When executable nodes and newly forced `skipped_by_guard` or `upstream_failed` nodes coexist, in what exact order are their actions and NodeExecution records produced, and is transitive propagation processed as one closure or in waves?
options: Choose the smallest `node_id` among all nodes whose next outcome is determined, whether execution, skip, or upstream failure.
Record the complete forced-conclusion closure first, then execute ready nodes.
Execute all ready nodes first, then materialize forced conclusions.
Propagate one graph-depth wave at a time, ordering each wave by node and map index.
open_points.default_guess: Choose the smallest identifier among all currently actionable nodes and apply one execution or forced conclusion at a time, recomputing afterward.

open_points.subject: guard skip versus a later upstream failure
open_points.text: A13 says an input that can no longer receive because its edges are disabled makes its node `skipped_by_guard`, says `upstream_failed` wins when both rules apply, and makes NodeExecution records immutable.
open_points.question: If one required input is already permanently disabled by a guard while another required input is still waiting and later fails, is the node skipped immediately, held undecided so it can become `upstream_failed`, or decided by whichever condition becomes known first?
options: Skip immediately; the later failure cannot change the immutable result.
Wait for all remaining upstream inputs, then use `upstream_failed` if any failed.
Use whichever condition is observed first, making request timing affect the result.
open_points.default_guess: Wait until remaining upstream inputs have concluded, then apply `upstream_failed` precedence if any failed.
